title: Topic 2.1: The Inspired Word of God

pages.lesson:
LESSON: THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.1: The Inspired Word of God

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Inspired Word of God. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you respect the Holy Bible?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the books in the Old and New Testament
2. role play naming some books in the Bible
3. recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Inspired Word of God helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD
Study The Inspired Word of God like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the books in the Old and New Testament

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the books in the Old and New Testament. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the books in the Old and New Testament.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the books in the Old and New Testament. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Role play naming some books in the Bible

What this means
In this part you learn to role play naming some books in the Bible. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: role play naming some books in the Bible.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Inspired Word of God in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can role play naming some books in the Bible. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always

What this means
In this part you learn to recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Inspired Word of God is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the books in the Old and New Testament)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Inspired Word of God in your own words. (skill: role play naming some books in the Bible)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Inspired Word of God to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the books in the Old and New Testament.
3. Practise this skill: role play naming some books in the Bible.
4. Practise this skill: recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always.
5. Make one local Kenya example of The Inspired Word of God from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Inspired Word of God: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study The Inspired Word of God?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you respect the Holy Bible?
2. Why is it important to know the books in the Holy Bible?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Inspired Word of God means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the books in the Old and New Testament.
5. Be able to: role play naming some books in the Bible.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
